title: Date-aware deeplink for cross-midnight deferred intervention cards
description: Intervention cards generated between quiet-hours start and midnight defer their push to next-day quiet-hours end (AnchorResolver.interventionFireMinute), but the card's own message_date stays the generation day. GET /api/proactive/feed?date= only returns the LOCAL today's rows, so the deep-linked /today?n=<id8> push from a next-morning push cannot surface the card on /today — the 'Segitett?' verdict chips are unreachable for that card. Fix: make the deeplink/feed lookup date-aware (e.g. resolve by card id directly, or have /today accept a date param and fetch across the boundary) so a deferred card's chips are reachable from the push that announces it. See docs/features/_platform-notifications.md sec 3d (mezo-b3pp.19 final-review finding 2).

title: Graph reinforcement bump may permanently saturate pattern-node edges toward 1.0
description:
Follow-up from mezo-b3pp.10's final whole-branch review (GraphMaintenanceService final review, 2026-08-23).

PatternDetectionService writes a fresh 'snapshot' pattern_event for a confirmed pattern on essentially every nightly run where the pair's gate verdict is LIVE — not just when something changed. GraphMaintenanceService.reinforceFreshPatterns treats any snapshot from the last 24h as 'fresh evidence' and bumps every edge touching that pattern's promoted node by graph.reinforcement-bump (default 0.05), capped at 1.0.

Arithmetic: nightly decay removes 0.01 x weight; reinforcement adds a flat 0.05. The bump wins at every weight in [0,1] (5x at w=1.0, 25x at w=0.2). So every edge touching a promoted PATTERN node ratchets to the 1.0 cap within roughly ten nights and stays there as long as the pattern keeps snapshotting. Since these are the hub nodes GraphEdgeStructurer hangs most edges off, graph.prune-floor can never reclaim them and traversal's weight ordering degenerates toward a flat 1.0 tier for the busiest part of the graph.

This matches spec section 6.5 literally ('fresh pattern evidence bumps its node's edges +0.05 capped at 1.0') and is not a bug in the current slice — CompanionProperties.Graph's own javadoc frames the bump as decay's 'counterweight', which implies balance rather than saturation though.

Worth revisiting once the graph has run for a while (lived-with evidence, same spirit as the W2 gate decision). Two candidate fixes if the ratchet turns out to be unwanted:
1. Require the snapshot to differ materially from the previous one before counting as 'fresh' (PatternDetectionService.recordSnapshot already loads the previous snapshot for its band-crossing check, so the signal is close at hand).
2. Scale the reinforcement bump by (1 - currentWeight) so it decays as the edge approaches the cap, rather than applying a flat bump.

Files: backend/src/main/java/io/mrkuhne/mezo/feature/companion/graph/service/GraphMaintenanceService.java (reinforceFreshPatterns), backend/src/main/java/io/mrkuhne/mezo/feature/companion/service/PatternDetectionService.java (recordSnapshot / the nightly snapshot-write cadence).

comments.author: mrkuhne
comments.text:
VERIFICATION (2026-08-31, no code change — the bd asks for lived-with evidence and that is not available: no persistent dev DB is running, and a dev/demo DB would not be lived-with evidence anyway). What I DID verify against the shipped code, so the eventual decision starts from a checked premise rather than an assumed one:

1. THE ARITHMETIC HOLDS, and the ratchet is CERTAIN rather than hypothetical. Per night an edge touching a fresh-snapshot pattern node goes w -> min(1, 0.99w + 0.05) (application.yml: decay-factor 0.99, reinforcement-bump 0.05). The fixed point of 0.99w + 0.05 = w is w = 5.0 — far above the 1.0 cap — so the cap always binds and saturation is guaranteed while snapshots keep arriving. The bd's '~ten nights' is right for mid-range weights (from w=0.5: ~12 nights) but optimistic at the low end (from w=0.2: ~19 nights). Edges are born at confidence x 0.5, so real starting weights are <=0.5.

2. THE LOAD-BEARING PREMISE HOLDS. PatternDetectionService.recordSnapshot writes a KIND_SNAPSHOT pattern_event UNCONDITIONALLY on every LIVE evaluation — the previous-snapshot lookup it performs is used only for the band-crossing notification, NOT to gate the write — and line ~116 calls it on every detection run for a CONFIRMED pattern. So a confirmed, still-correlating pattern does get a fresh snapshot every night, which is exactly what GraphMaintenanceService.reinforceFreshPatterns treats as fresh evidence.

3. CANDIDATE FIX 2 CHECKS OUT ARITHMETICALLY. Scaling the bump by (1 - w) gives w -> 0.94w + 0.05, whose fixed point is 0.05/0.06 = 0.833 — below the cap, so weight ordering survives: a recently reinforced edge sits at ~0.833 while an unreinforced one keeps decaying past it. It preserves the reinforcement signal instead of removing it, and needs no new tuning knob. It does depart from spec section 6.5's literal wording ('+0.05 capped at 1.0'), which is why it is a product decision, not a bugfix.

STILL OPEN, deliberately: whether the resulting flat-1.0 tier actually degrades the [Osszefuggesek] block enough to matter. That is the part only lived-with usage can answer, and it is the same spirit as the W2 gate decision. Re-check when the graph has real history: 'select weight, count(*) from knowledge_edge where is_deleted=false group by weight order by weight desc' — a mass at exactly 1.000 is the signal.

close_reason: GlobalExceptionHandler.handleTypeMismatch: MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException -> 400 FIELD VALIDATION_INVALID_VALUE a paraméter nevével. A konverzió a controller-metódus ÉS a bean validation előtt fut, tehát ez az egyetlen réteg, ami elkaphatja; eddig a generikus Exception catch-all vitte 500-ra. TDD: GlobalExceptionHandlerIT 3 teszt (rossz UUID path param, nem szám query param, plusz a 404-es út őrzése — jó formátumú ismeretlen UUID továbbra is LLM_LOG_CALL_NOT_FOUND). Regresszió 520 teszt, CI teljes suite zöld. A kliens értéke szándékosan nem kerül a válaszba, csak a logba a trace id mellé. Következmény: az enum típusú query-paraméterek mostantól biztonságosak a kontraktusban; a mezo-uakh pattern-stringjei maradnak (működnek, kétszeresen validáltak), a kényszer szűnt meg. title: Unread MezoChip dot can re-appear on an already-read thread
description:
Cosmetic bug, low reachability. In TodayPage.tsx (~line 326-327), the unread-dot logic is:

  const latestId = messages.length > 0 ? messages[messages.length - 1].id : null
  const msgsUnread = latestId != null && latestId !== seenId

messages comes from buildMezoMessages({ briefing, note, briefingDemo }) (features/today/logic/mezoMessages.ts), which pushes at most two entries with FIXED ids: 'briefing' (if a briefing exists) then 'note' (if a same-day CompanionNote exists), in that order. latestId is simply the id of the last pushed entry — 'note' when a note is present, else 'briefing'.

Repro sequence:
1. Both a briefing and a companion note exist for today. Thread's latest id is 'note'.
2. User opens MezoMessagesSheet -> openMessages() calls markMessagesSeen(date, 'note') and setSeenId('note') (shared/lib/seenMessages.ts). Dot clears.
3. Later in the SAME day, useCompanionNote() (data/today/heartbeatHooks.ts or equivalent) starts returning null again — e.g. a nudge/closing note's time window closes, or a refetch drops it for any other reason (the hook is not guaranteed monotonic within a day).
4. buildMezoMessages now only pushes the briefing entry. latestId flips back to 'briefing'.
5. msgsUnread = ('briefing' !== 'note') = true -> the coral unread dot re-appears on MezoChip even though nothing new was said and the user already read everything that's currently showing.

Root cause: the unread comparison keys off a small FIXED id ('briefing'/'note') rather than a value that is monotonic/stable across a note appearing-then-disappearing within the same day (e.g. a count, a hash of the thread content, or "seen" tracked per-id-that-existed rather than "seen == single latest id").

Suggested fix directions (not prescriptive): track a set/count of seen ids instead of a single latestId scalar, or don't let the unread signal go from false back to true within the same day once the note that produced 'note' disappears (only compare against ids that are STILL present, or treat a shrinking thread as never re-arming unread).

Non-goals: this is UI-cosmetic only, no data loss, no write-path involved. Low priority (P3) - the note transitioning from present to absent within the same day is an edge case (proactive heartbeat notes are typically time-window-gated, not click-to-dismiss), but it IS reachable, e.g. mock scenario switches or a real-mode refetch racing a window boundary.

Found during the mezo-e26w today-ios-redesign fix wave pre-merge review (2026-08-12). Files: frontend/src/features/today/pages/TodayPage.tsx:319-334, frontend/src/features/today/logic/mezoMessages.ts, frontend/src/shared/lib/seenMessages.ts.

notes: Investigated 2026-08-08 (PR #157): only train-session light+dark still drifted (train-gym re-baselined by a later commit). Root cause: darwin goldens predated the Heti zóna-kontextus prep card (live-zone-unify) + mezo-oyhy.3 estimateSessionMinutes pill change (~78 -> ~53 perc). The ['train','weekWorkouts'] 'No queryFn was passed' console error is benign: dev-only React Query useBaseQuery warning for the intentional enabled:false queryFn-less cache observer in weekMuscleLogHooks.ts (fires on observer mount even when disabled; never fetches). Measured with Playwright's own comparator: the 78->53 digit swap = 305 diff px on darwin (>120 tolerance) but <120 on linux — so the LINUX train-session golden still carries the stale ~78 pill and CI stays green; it will fold into the next legit linux regen.

title: Extract the duplicated exercise-identity resolution (3 copies)
description: Follow-up from the medal-collection final review (mezo-wp6n, PR #110). The exercise-identity resolution block ('c:'+catalogId else 'n:'+name, over findIdentityRowsIncludingDeleted, plus the catalog display merge) now exists verbatim in THREE places: ExerciseRecordService, MedalService, and GymSignalCalculator. Identity semantics are a load-bearing invariant - soft-deleted day-edit rows must still count, or a plan edit silently erases history - and it now has to be changed in three files in lockstep. Pre-existing pattern, not introduced by the medal work; the medal slice made it a three-way rather than two-way duplication.

Not a regression (it never passed hadPR either) and the /train/medals cabinet covers the history, but the review page is where you would look for one specific session. Needs WorkoutDetailResponse to carry medals[] (MedalService.forSession already computes exactly this), then pass them through.

title: Medal XP: SESSION_VOLUME records pay prBonusXp into max_strength
description: Follow-up from the medal-collection final review (mezo-wp6n, PR #110). ProgressionService.applyGym counts all four RECORD-tier medal types into recordMedalCount, so a SESSION_VOLUME record pays prBonusXp (40) into max_strength. Volume climbs weekly by design in an accumulation block, making SESSION_VOLUME the most frequently firing record type - so most exercises earn one most weeks, landing ~6x40 XP of volume-driven bonus in a strength skill. Two problems: max_strength is semantically the wrong skill for a volume record, and the single pr-bonus-xp knob cannot be tuned down for volume without also devaluing WEIGHT/E1RM. This matches the spec exactly (2026-07-30-medal-collection-design.md sections 6 and 7.3) so it is a design consequence, not drift, and the economy is display-only.
design: Options: (a) exclude SESSION_VOLUME from recordMedalCount; (b) give it its own smaller property and route it to a volume-ish skill; (c) leave it and accept faster max_strength progression. Decide by watching whether max_strength levels start outpacing the other athletic skills.

title: Make the NOVA-freeze test actually discriminate (it passes against the pre-fix code too)
description:
MealOverridesIT.testCreate_shouldKeepTheFrozenNova_whenAnOverrideOnlyChangesAnAmount (added in mezo-ormb's final fix wave) asserts the right value but cannot fail against the pre-fix implementation. The pre-fix code ran dominantNova() whenever ANY override existed; since the test never drifts pantry data between recipe-save and meal-log, that live read lands on the same max(1,4)=4 the frozen novaDominant holds. Both implementations pass.

To make it discriminate, soft-delete (or edit the nova of) the high-NOVA pantry item AFTER creating the recipe and BEFORE logging: DELETE /api/pantry/{id} is a soft delete (is_deleted = true), so the recipe_ingredient FK RESTRICT does not block it, and dominantNova's findAllById + @SQLRestriction then cannot resolve that row. Expected: pre-fix -> NOVA 1 (the live read loses the deleted syrup); post-fix -> NOVA 4 (the frozen novaDominant is kept because no line was dropped to 0). Verify the mutation by temporarily reverting MealService's anyLineDropped ternary to overrides.isEmpty() and confirming the test goes red.

Related: mezo-6xnf (freeze per-line NOVA on recipe_ingredient) would make this whole class of drift impossible.
notes: Correction: the sibling issue referenced in this description as 'mezo-6xnf' is actually mezo-4tzf (freeze per-line NOVA on recipe_ingredient). The wrong id was a guess that also landed in commit bd37511c's message and cannot be corrected there without rewriting main's history.

title: Freeze per-line NOVA on recipe_ingredient so a logged meal's snapshotNova never depends on live pantry rows
description:
Found by the mezo-ormb final whole-branch review. MealService.buildItem picks snapshotNova as: overrides.isEmpty() ? recipe.getNovaDominant() (FROZEN at recipe-save) : dominantNova(recipe, overrides) (LIVE pantry_item.nova via findAllById, which @SQLRestriction filters for soft-deletes). recipe_ingredient stores no per-line nova, so the live read was forced.

mezo-ormb narrowed the trigger: the live recompute now runs only when a line is actually dropped to 0 (that is the only case where the SET of contributing ingredients changes, so the only case where the dominant NOVA can move). A non-zero amount change now keeps the frozen value. That removes the 'an unrelated override flips nova semantics' bug.

Residual: if a line IS zeroed AND another line's pantry row was since soft-deleted or had its nova edited, the recomputed dominant still reflects live data rather than what was eaten. Fix properly by adding recipe_ingredient.snapshot_nova (captured in RecipeService.buildLine alongside the other snapshot* fields) and computing the dominant from the frozen per-line values in BOTH branches.
acceptance_criteria: snapshotNova on a logged meal is derived only from values frozen at recipe-save time; editing or soft-deleting a pantry item afterwards cannot change any already-logged meal's snapshotNova, with or without overrides.
notes: Note: commit bd37511c's message and PR #107 originally referenced this issue as 'mezo-6xnf' — an id guessed before the real one was read back. THIS (mezo-4tzf) is the real issue; the commit message is immutable on main.

title: [flake] ActiveWorkoutPage.test.tsx real-mode tests time out locally (5000ms) — reproduces on clean origin/main
description:

Verified on a clean origin/main checkout (7ec9e81a) in an isolated worktree: it fails there too, so it is NOT caused by any feature branch. The failing subset varies run to run (2 failed/65 passed on one run, a different single test on another), which is the signature of timing sensitivity under machine load rather than a logic defect. All failures are in the file's real-mode group (e.g. 'real mode: a hard reload on /train/session resumes instead of redirecting while queries load', ActiveWorkoutPage.test.tsx:756).

Worth deciding: raise testTimeout for that file's real-mode group, or make the queries deterministic so the test does not depend on wall-clock. CI (clean ubuntu-latest) may or may not reproduce it — check a recent ci.yml 'Tests (real mode)' leg before investing.

title: Expose the recipe line's frozen per-basis rate so the FE can mirror the backend exactly on overridden lines
description:
Surfaced by the mezo-ormb Task 6 review. The backend computes every recipe line from RecipeIngredientEntity's FROZEN snapshotPer/snapshotKcal/... captured when the recipe was last saved; there is no re-snapshot mechanism. The frontend cannot see those values — RecipeIngredientResponse exposes only 'contribution' (the already-rounded macro share AT the line's stored amount) and no per-basis rate.

mezo-ormb mitigated most of the exposure: computeRecipeMacrosWithOverrides now reuses the server-frozen 'contribution' for every UNTOUCHED line. But an OVERRIDDEN line has no frozen rate on the wire for its new amount, so it is rescaled from the LIVE pantry row. If that pantry item's macros changed after the recipe was saved, the log sheet's preview for that one line disagrees with what the server freezes on save.

Fix: add the frozen per-basis rate to RecipeIngredientResponse (contract-first) — 'per' (snapshotPer), 'basisUnit', and the per-basis macros — map them in RecipeMapper.toIngredientResponse, carry them into the FE RecipeIngredientLine type and recipeApi.fromResponse, populate them in the mock seed's enrichLine, then have computeRecipeMacrosWithOverrides scale overridden lines from the frozen rate instead of the live pantry row. Deriving an implied rate from contribution/amount is NOT a valid shortcut: 'contribution' is already rounded to whole numbers, so it loses precision (snapshot 110/100g at 3 g -> contribution 3 -> implied 1.0/g -> at 6 g gives 6, while the backend gives 7).
acceptance_criteria: An overridden line's previewed macros equal what the backend freezes, even when the referenced pantry item's macros changed after the recipe was last saved. Covered by a test that drifts the live pantry row and asserts the overridden line still scales from the frozen rate.
notes: Final-review widening (mezo-ormb): the blast radius is bigger than 'the preview can differ when macros drifted'. When an overridden line's pantry row is UNRESOLVABLE (soft-deleted — PantryService.deleteItem has no in-use guard), the FE previewed that line as 0 while the backend still scales it from the recipe's frozen snapshot and never consults the pantry at all. mezo-ormb mitigated this by rescaling the wire's frozen 'contribution' in that fallback, which is lossy (the frozen value is pre-rounded) but far closer than 0. The full fix is still to put the frozen per-basis rate on RecipeIngredientResponse so an overridden line scales exactly like the server.

title: Notification preview copy mirrors hardcoded minutes instead of the resolved anchor
description: After the N2 fix wave moved memoir/midday/weekly anchors past their generator's cron (prose-generation-grace-min: 15), two frontend spots still hardcode the OLD minute: NOTIFICATION_CATEGORY_META's memoir description ('Vasarnap este 19:00' — the anchor is now 19:15) and notificationForecast.ts's MIDDAY_HHMM / MEMOIR_HHMM mirrors. The sparkline buckets by hour so only the memoir sub-line and the dense-window minute labels are off by 15 minutes; nothing sends at the wrong time (the backend anchor is authoritative). Deliberately NOT fixed in the wave: re-hardcoding a now-config-derived minute into Hungarian user copy would recreate exactly the duplication FIX 2 removed. Proper fix: serve the resolved anchor minute to the FE (e.g. include it in the pref response, or a small GET that returns today's due-time list) and let the sub-lines + forecast read it, so there is one source of truth for the minute.

title: Train Mai polish follow-ups from the mezo-9bbc final review
description:
Three residual items parked at the end of mezo-9bbc's final review (all Low, none blocking that merge):

1. dayStripItems' isToday is still flag-based (features/train/logic/dayStripItems.ts, reads d.isToday). After mezo-9bbc made TrainTodayPage's isTodayShown date-based, a real-mode rest or run-only day now correctly renders 'Mai nap' while NO DayStrip chip is marked MA, wears the coral .today border, or says '· ma' in its aria-label. Same class of bug as the fixed one, one surface further out.

2. Latent mock-only date trap: TrainTodayPage omits the sheet date when shownIso === todayIso, and the mock sport mutation then falls back to localDateString(). If the mock fixture's flagged 'today' (Csü) ever gains a sport slot, that log would be dated the real weekday and the card would not flip to MEGVAN. Unreachable today (no Csü sport slot; the schedule mutation is a mock no-op).

3. Stale comments at TrainTodayPage.tsx (around the todayRow/isTodayShown derivation and the DayStrip selected fallback) still claim shownDay can be undefined on a real-mode rest day. The C2 calendar fallback made that impossible, so they describe a dead path and the selected={... ?? DAY_ORDER[todayIdx()]} fallback is unreachable.

Also noted: I1 (cross/TRX tone on Heti rows) ships with no visual-golden coverage, because the mock week's sport slots carry no sport discriminator so every slot resolves to volleyball. A mock fixture with a cross or TRX slot would give the golden suite teeth there.

title: RecipeEditorPage draft state seeds once, before a cold real-mode load resolves
description: RecipeEditorPage seeds its whole draft (name, slot, starred, servings, prep/cook, tags, lines and - since mezo-uavr - role) from useState first-render initializers reading editing = recipes.find(id). On a cold real-mode deep link to /fuel/recipes/:id/edit the ['recipes'] query has not resolved on first render, so editing is undefined and every field seeds to its default; when the list lands, the guard's 'Nincs ilyen recept.' fallback goes away but the draft stays blank. Today the whole draft is blank in that state (so it is visibly wrong rather than silently wrong) and the page is normally reached by navigation from the detail page with a warm cache - which is why this was accepted as pre-existing rather than a mezo-uavr regression. Fix the pattern once for the whole form: either block the editor render until the recipe resolves, or re-seed from editing in an effect keyed on its id. Found during mezo-uavr Task 7 review.

title: Mock recipe seed has no post_workout recipe
description: frontend/src/data/fuel/mockRecipes seeds role: 'pre_workout' (rec-1 / the MSW recipeFixture) and 'standard' everywhere else, so the 'Edzes utan' role label never renders in mock mode - not the detail hero chip, not the library card tag, not the PONTSZAM rubric note ('edzes utani merce szerint'), not the editor's third segment in a seeded-edit state. Mock mode is the offline demo + the both-modes test surface, so a whole third of the mezo-uavr feature is invisible there. Also inconsistent: seed rec-2 / rec-4 are slot/tag-labelled pre-workout yet carry role standard, which reads like a bug to anyone browsing the seed. Fix: give one seed recipe role: 'post_workout' and align the pre-workout-labelled seeds with their role. Found during mezo-uavr Tasks 6 and 8 review.

title: PRE_WORKOUT prose prompt invites blaming protein
description: RecipeBreakdownProseService.java:126-127 ends the PRE_WORKOUT role block with '(a feherje/zsir-dominancia itt gyengebb illeszkedes)'. That phrasing invites the LLM to write protein down as a fault, contradicting the pre-existing macro rule elsewhere in the same prompt ('tobblet-feherjet sose rodd fel hibakent'). The honest framing of the same fact is scarcity-of-carbs, not excess-of-protein: 'keves a szenhidrat a szerephez'. Deterministically the score is identical either way (the pre_workout macro target is carb-heavy, so a protein/fat-dominant recipe scores lower under it) - this is purely about the prose not blaming the wrong nutrient. Update the copy and the RecipeBreakdownProseServiceTest assertion that pins it. Flagged in mezo-uavr Task 5 review as 'fix in a later wave'.

title: a11y: Fuel segmented controls need radiogroup semantics

See the accessibility-patterns skill for the radiogroup/roving-tabindex recipe. Found during mezo-uavr Task 7 review.

title: Pantry writes must invalidate the recipe-derived caches
description: usePantryActions.invalidate() (frontend/src/data/fuel/pantryHooks.ts:52) only invalidates ['pantry']. A pantry macro edit therefore silently changes every recipe's deterministic fit + template breakdown server-side (RecipeBreakdownService recomputes on read and regenerates the prose when the numbers no longer match) while the FE keeps serving the ['recipes'] / ['recipeBreakdown'] caches until they happen to refetch. Two consequences: (1) the recipe library badge + the detail score sheet show a pre-edit fit; (2) the mezo-uavr refreshing flag never fires for this path, so the honest 'Mezo ujraertekeli a receptet...' banner is skipped and the stale prose swaps in silently on the next refetch. Fix: add qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['recipes'] }) and qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['recipeBreakdown'] }) to the pantry write invalidation (mirroring useRecipeActions, which already invalidates ['pantry']). Then correct the recipeHooks JSDoc, which currently states this path is NOT an invalidation, and docs/features/fuel.md. Found during mezo-uavr Task 9 review.
notes: Shipped in PR #93 (merge 2393713e, live v0.139.1). Scoped twice over: only the recipes whose lines reference the edited item, and only when a fact the scorer re-reads live changed (NOVA, fiber/sugar/salt/sat-fat, category, basis) — a recipe's macros are frozen in its line snapshots, so a price or kcal edit moves nothing. delete always invalidates referencing recipes; add/import touches no recipe cache. Query keys extracted to data/fuel/queryKeys.ts (the invalidation is mutual).

title: [bug] Recipe editor: a line for a since-deleted pantry item shows UUID + 0 macros (seed snapshot name/contribution into DraftLine)
description: Pre-existing (predates mezo-yew, surfaced by the adversarial review of that fix). In RecipeEditorView edit mode, a recipe line whose pantry item was soft-deleted no longer resolves against usePantry().ingredients → row renders line.refId (UUID) + contributionOf(line, undefined)=0, and zero-drags the live MAKRO-OSSZEG. The data to fix this already exists: the backend persists snapshotName + snapshot macros on recipe_ingredient, and recipeApi.fromResponse carries them onto RecipeIngredientLine.name/.contribution — but the editor's DraftLine seed (RecipeEditorView.tsx ~line 79) discards both. Fix: carry name (and contribution) into DraftLine, and fall back to the snapshot name when usePantry() resolution misses; the live editor cannot recompute contributions for a missing ingredient, so for a deleted item show the frozen snapshot contribution at the stored amount (and consider disabling the stepper for that orphan line). Low priority: requires soft-deleting a pantry item still referenced by a saved recipe, no data corruption (amounts/refIds preserved on save) — only a misleading display until re-pick.

title: Doc-lint staleness: growth.md, ritual.md, insights.md
description: node scripts/lint-docs.mjs reports 3 stale feature docs. Verified NOT caused by the push-N1 branch: growth.md (quest 2026-07-26, activity 2026-07-28) and ritual.md (data/ritual 2026-07-26) predate it; insights.md is flagged only because frontend/src/data/hooks.ts appears in its key_files and N1 added one re-export line to it — coarse-detector fan-out, no Insights pointer moved. CI is unaffected (ci.yml runs lint-docs --errors-only, 0 errors). Either refresh the three docs against their real drift, or reconsider whether a shared file like data/hooks.ts belongs in per-domain key_files at all — that fan-out will keep producing false staleness on every barrel edit.

title: Fuel Mai: polish + test-coverage follow-ups from the mezo-rrtj final review
description:
Non-blocking items triaged out of the mezo-rrtj final whole-branch review:
- heroWindow.deriveWhy's final empty-string branch (a now-slot with no kcal) is untested; the consumer guards {why && ...} so behaviour is safe.
- NowWindowCard repeats its .top/.lbl/.dot header markup across the open/closed branches (2 lines, differing content) - extract only if a third hero variant appears.
- MissedStrip renders an unrequested aria-hidden warning glyph (cosmetic, matches the mockup).
- DayZoneCard has parallel three-way ternaries over zone.state (stateCls/kcalSuffix) - a single STATE_META lookup would read better.
- No test asserts the header Reta strip navigates to /fuel/gyogyszer.
- MissedStrip's page-level wiring has no integration test (the fixed 13:30 mock never yields a missed window; needs the injectOpenSlot idiom).
- FuelMaiPage's water quick-add assertion passes regardless of whether the click incremented consumed.water (the increment is proven at component level).
- WCAG 2.5.3 label-in-name: the Reta button's visible text ('Fuel · Reta D3') is not contained in its aria-label ('Reta ciklus megnyitasa').

title: Fuel Mai: log-success motion (zone count-up + hero slide-morph to the next window)
description: Deliberately out of scope for mezo-rrtj: after a successful log the zone header kcal should count up, the row should flash sage with a check pop, the daily 'hatra' number should tick down, and the hero should slide up and morph to the NEXT window so the guidance continues. Needs transition state the page does not hold today. Spec section 5 (Motion) marks these as follow-ups; the entry animations (hero pulse, zone stagger, bar grow, chip pop) already shipped.

title: Fuel: remove the now-unconsumed FuelDay.pacing / .micronutrients fields
description: After mezo-rrtj no surface renders either field; they stay typed + seeded only because data-layer tests pin the FuelDay shape (fuelHooks.test.tsx, fuelData.test.tsx). Once mezo's day-level coach line and the weekly micro rollup land in their real homes, drop both fields from FuelDay, the seed and those tests. Spec section 8.3.

title: chore(train): mezo-05v6 deferred minors — sport-slot polish batch
description: Final-review demoted findings from feat/sport-schedule-discriminator: (1) contract wording: SportScheduleSlot sport described as 'Sport discriminator' vs sibling SportSession 'Modality discriminator' — align (touches generated files). (2) No server-side enforcement of kind='training' for non-volleyball slots (raw client can PUT trx+match; FE renders 'meccs' and coerces back on next editor save) — consider service guard or DB CHECK. (3) SportPage weeklyHours renders raw JS number (2.5h dot) vs LoadTiles hu-comma (6,5h) — share a hoursHu-style helper. (4) Editor polish: role=group aria-label wraps the delete button; key={si} index keys (stable slot ids would close a theoretical uncommitted-draft migration on removal); no 'cross' kind test; no multi-slot-removal reindex test. (5) LoadTiles: no two-co-existing-sport-tiles render test. (6) UX decision: MA chip renders per slot on today (two slots = two MA tags). (7) Known limitation to document: two same-sport slots on one day share done-state (date+sport matching only, no schedule-log link — relates mezo-0p3).

title: E4 — Shop + coins (future): wallet ledger, shop UI, coin visibility, spendable items
description: Parked fourth epic of gamified growth (umbrella mezo-52vz, spec §6/§10 E4). Prepared groundwork already on main: reward envelope {xp, coins} in quest catalog + daily_quest.coins column (always 0, invisible). Principles recorded in spec §6 + ADR 0010: XP = permanent progress, never spendable; coins = spendable on convenience/cosmetic only (extra reroll, quest swap, themes); never pay-to-win, never real money; coins ship TOGETHER with the shop (an unspendable currency is a broken promise). Needs its own brainstorm/design before implementation.

title: Catalog: de-dup catalog→video resolve + multi-user setVideo scoping
description: (a) The ~6-line catalogIds→video-map resolve is duplicated across WorkoutService.getToday and TrainService.videosByCatalog — extract a shared helper. (b) Forward-looking (single-user moot today): setVideo/list are not owner-scoped → in a multi-user world setVideo is an IDOR on any row's video_url and slug-gen is check-then-insert (race). Harden when multi-user lands. Whole-branch review #6 + forward-looking.

title: data: migrate domain interfaces out of shared data/types.ts into per-domain types
FE: owner token bootstrap fires twice on page load (duplicate /api/auth/login)
description: Observed during live browser verification: loading /train/mesocycles in real mode issues TWO parallel POST /api/auth/login requests (both 200) — the two TanStack queries (mesocycles + sport-sessions) likely race the token bootstrap. Harmless (idempotent login) but doubles auth traffic on cold load. Consider memoizing the in-flight bootstrap promise in lib/api.ts.
